Although the speaker discusses possible price increases and longer-term buying opportunities, the video also describes a possible 20 to 50 percent decline and says it is too soon to be completely bullish, without requiring viewers to purchase, pay, or provide data.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker connects a purchase decision to an expected gain: he says he will “buy the Depp one by one” because he expects “great moves on the upside” by the end of the cycle. He then calls the current price area a place where he is “willing to buy a lot.” This is more than a detached forecast. The audience is given a model for buying AVAX now and a reason to expect appreciation from doing so.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that a decline is discussed, but the speaker immediately turns that risk into a purchase rationale, calling such declines “great great buying opportunities.” His warning about being too bullish concerns the present signal; it does not undo the longer-term buy-and-appreciation message. Nor does the absence of a payment instruction settle whether the video steers viewers toward buying the token.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited buying statement describes what the speaker personally intends to do, not an instruction or pathway for viewers to purchase AVAX. The upside view is an opinion within a conditional analysis that also contemplates substantial losses and says it is too soon to be fully bullish. Those qualifications matter: an investment thesis, even an enthusiastic one, does not by itself establish a deceptive solicitation.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the cumulative pitch. The title says AVAX is “EXPLODING,” the speaker calls the developer numbers “very very bullish,” and he says he expects “great moves on the upside.” Even a possible further drop becomes, in his telling, a “great great buying” opportunity. That combination makes nearly every price direction serve the case for buying: strength validates the thesis, while weakness offers an entry. The risk disclosure is real, but it is packaged inside a persistently favorable purchase narrative.

by the end of this cycle we are going to witness some great moves on the upside

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to uncertainty, but uncertainty is folded into the same favorable conclusion: the stated worst-case decline is followed by a description of further losses as buying opportunities. Saying it is too soon to be completely bullish narrows the short-term chart call; it does not neutralize the broader message that weakness favors accumulating AVAX.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Strong language in a title and an optimistic thesis are not evidence of a scam on their own. The speaker gives a concrete downside scenario, identifies a bearish signal that would imply continued decline, and makes greater bullish confidence conditional on a later price move. The opening highlights enthusiasm but does not show a guaranteed return, a deceptive mechanism, or a viewer purchase instruction.

opening.argument: Judge, the chart tutorial also functions as a case for owning AVAX. The speaker moves from developer-activity figures to the claim that the chain has more retail adoption, then identifies AVAX as a project he expects to perform well. The chart discussion culminates in his willingness to buy a lot around current levels. Those steps turn ostensibly educational material into a token-appreciation narrative with a concrete buying example, even though it is expressed as personal analysis.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Listing chart indicators does not make the purchase message incidental. The defense itself cites the speaker's upside expectation and his description of declines as buying opportunities. The dispute is how those observations function together: the statistics establish the favorable story, while the price discussion supplies the moment to act on it. Explicitly requiring payment in the video is not the only way to encourage a token purchase.

citations.quote: by the end of this cycle we are going to witness some great moves on the upside

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The opening describes a bullish investment thesis, but its citations do not establish deceptive promotion or a participation pathway. The speaker marks the adoption inference as opinion, examines competing chart interpretations, and tells viewers to wait for further signals before becoming fully bullish. Personal willingness to buy does not convert that conditional market discussion into a scam.
